title: Lawyers Roundtable: Is the Sovereign Citizen movement legit?
summary: Three lawyers react to sovereign-citizen traffic-stop videos and explain why the right-to-travel, corporation and opt-out arguments fail.

assertions.quote: the truth is of course you need a driver's license about driver's license to operate a motor vehicle in the United States of America
I don't know how they came up with that but it is not supported by the law

verdicts.note: Motor vehicle codes define driving as operating a vehicle on public roads regardless of purpose; courts reject the commerce distinction.

assertions.quote: because the U.S government is not a corporation I think that's the Crux of their argument

verdicts.note: The Supreme Court distinguishes the District's municipal corporation from the sovereign US government, in which the District's sovereign power is lodged; it does not treat the federal government as a corporation.

A district court held the United States is a sovereign, not a corporation, and called contrary arguments wholly frivolous; the Tax Court sanctioned a taxpayer arguing 'the United States is a corporation'; trial-level rulings.

assertions.quote: absent that you're never winning this on a legal basis
it never works except for um when a prosecutor gets annoyed and it's like this is a stupid ticket anyways fine just go away
at the very core it is desperation it is people who are getting arrested and want a way out
I don't see any reason why he couldn't walk and go get lunch

verdicts.note: Drivers must show a licence and passengers generally need not identify absent reasonable suspicion, but stop-and-identify laws and officer-safety orders vary by state.
